report:
**Conclusion**  
Yes, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy effectively alleviates the symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

**Evidence Behind the Conclusion**
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Data from randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses show that EMDR therapy leads to meaningful improvements in PTSD diagnoses, substantial reductions in core PTSD symptoms, and decreases in related psychological distress (https://www.academia.edu/24594286/The_relationship_between_efficacy_and_methodology_in_studies_investigating_EMDR_treatment_of_PTSD).
* **Comparative Effectiveness:** Systematic reviews indicate that the therapeutic efficacy of EMDR for adults with PTSD is equivalent to other established trauma-focused treatments, such as Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) and Prolonged Exposure (PE) therapy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_movement_desensitization_and_reprocessing).
* **Global Medical Consensus:** Leading international health and psychological organizations recognize EMDR as an evidence-based intervention:
  * The **World Health Organization (WHO)** highlights EMDR alongside trauma-focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) as having the strongest evidence base for effective PTSD treatment (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/post-traumatic-stress-disorder).
  * The **American Psychological Association (APA)** includes EMDR among its recommended treatments in clinical practice guidelines for adult PTSD (https://www.apa.org/ptsd-guideline/treatments/eye-movement-reprocessing).
